name: tiny-tech

tools.name: tiny_whoami
tools.description: Who am I on tiny.technology? Returns identity and the list of tinys (AI personas) the user owns.

tools.name: tiny_login
tools.description: Log in to tiny.technology — opens the browser for a one-click authorization. Use when other tiny_* tools report auth errors.

tools.name: tiny_learn
tools.description: Store a durable memory about the user in tiny.technology's server-side memory graph (follows them across every agent and device — Claude Code today, their phone tomorrow). Keep entries short and factual, ≤2000 chars. When a new fact REPLACES an outdated one (moved, changed stack, new job), pass the old memory id in `supersedes` — it's closed as history, never deleted. When facts belong together, link them via `edges`.

supersedes.description: Memory ids this fact replaces (closed bitemporally, kept as history)

edges.description: Link this fact to existing memories — connected facts surface together in recall

dst.description: Existing memory id to link to

visibility.description: 'public' shares the fact with the user's followers (their feed). ONLY when the user explicitly asks to share/publish — default private

tools.name: tiny_recall
tools.description: Semantic search over everything tiny knows about the user (their cross-agent memory graph). Use at the start of tasks to pull relevant context, or when the user references something you don't know. hops=1 also walks graph edges so facts LINKED to the matches surface too — use when context matters (projects, relationships, threads).

hops.description: 1 = expand through graph edges to connected facts

tools.name: tiny_unlearn
tools.description: Close one memory by id (bitemporal: it leaves recall but survives as history — get ids from tiny_recall / tiny_memories), or ALL memories when id is omitted — confirm with the user before wiping everything.

id.description: Memory id; omit to close ALL memories

tools.name: tiny_memories
tools.description: List the user's most recent memories (no search — just the latest entries). include_history=true also returns closed (superseded/unlearned) facts with freshness fields.

tools.name: tiny_graph
tools.description: Explore the user's memory graph structure. mode 'neighbors': the subgraph around a memory id (which facts link to it, via which relations — supersedes trails, part_of clusters). mode 'conflicts': contradiction candidates (same subject+relation pointing at different facts in the same scope) — present them to the user, then tiny_resolve_conflict with their pick. mode 'social': the PUBLIC interaction graph around a node (user:<id> or tiny:<slug>) + trust scores (PageRank over tiny-consults-tiny edges). mode 'feed': fresh public facts from builders the user follows.

node.description: neighbors: a memory id · social: 'user:<id>' or 'tiny:<slug>' (optional — omit for trust scores only)

tools.name: tiny_resolve_conflict
tools.description: Resolve a memory contradiction found by tiny_graph mode 'conflicts': keep the edge the user chose as current, close the rest as history (bitemporal — nothing is deleted). ALWAYS ask the user which candidate is current before resolving.

keep.description: Edge id to keep live (from the conflict candidates)

close.description: Edge ids to close as history

tools.name: tiny_chat
tools.description: Send a message to one of the user's tinys (or any public tiny) and get the full agent response. The tiny runs server-side with its complete toolset — web http, sub-agent spawning, scheduling, telegram, semantic retrieval, the user's forged tools. Attach local images (jpg/png/gif/webp <3MB), documents (pdf/csv/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/html/xml) or text files via `files`. Use for anything a tiny is better positioned to do, or to consult a persona.

tiny.description: Tiny name, e.g. 'tiny' (the default assistant) or a custom persona

system_context.description: Optional extra context injected as a system message

tools.name: tiny_search
tools.description: Search the tiny.technology universe in one call: PEOPLE by partial @login or display name (e.g. "yak", "esra" → the exact @login that tiny_send_message / ask_tiny / sharing accept — use this whenever the user names a person and you lack their login; several matches → ask which, none → say so, never guess a login), TINYS by name prefix, and KNOWLEDGE by topic (semantic search over public tinys). Returns {people, tinys, knowledge}; a leg that failed carries {error} instead of an empty list. With neither query nor prefix: plain listing of public tinys.

query.description: Partial @login / name of a person, a tiny name, or a topic

prefix.description: Tiny-name prefix for the tinys leg (defaults to query)

tools.name: tiny_create_tool
tools.description: Forge a personal JavaScript tool that persists in the user's tiny account and follows them everywhere (web chat, telegram, this MCP server). Code shape: a single arrow function `(args) => result`. Sandbox: guarded fetch (https, public hosts; returns {status, ok, body} pre-parsed), JSON/Math/Date/String/URL, 10s timeout, ≤4KB. Code is PUBLIC on the user's builder profile — never embed secrets (pass them as args at call time). After creating, call tiny_reload_tools to mount it here.

params.description: Map of argName → description (all string args)

tools.name: tiny_remove_tool
tools.description: Delete one of the user's forged tools by name.

name.description: Tool name (with or without the my_ prefix)

tools.name: tiny_marketplace
tools.description: Browse public forged tools from the community, or install one from a builder into the user's account.

tools.name: mesh_peers
tools.description: List agents auto-discovered on the local zenoh mesh (tiny nodes + devduck instances on this LAN or connected endpoints): instance id, host, model, platform, cwd, tool count, freshness. Use before mesh_send to pick a target.

tools.name: mesh_send
tools.description: Send a command to ONE mesh peer (id from mesh_peers). That machine runs it through its own agent with ITS local tools — shell, screen, files — and returns the answer.

tools.name: mesh_broadcast
tools.description: Send a command to EVERY agent on the mesh and collect all answers. Fan-out work across the fleet (e.g. "how much disk is free?").

tools.name: tiny_reload_tools
tools.description: Re-sync the user's forged tools into this MCP session (call after tiny_create_tool / tiny_remove_tool / tiny_marketplace install).

tools.name: tiny_schedule
tools.description: Manage background jobs that run server-side on a schedule even when every device is off — results land on the user's event feed. Recurring: '*/30m', '*/2h', 'daily@09:00' (UTC). One-shot: run_in_minutes.

prompt.description: What the job does each run (create)

run_in_minutes.description: One-shot: run once N minutes from now

tiny.description: Tiny persona to run the job as (default: tiny)

tools.name: tiny_share
tools.description: Conversation share links. action:'create' publishes a snapshot ({role, content} messages) as a short tiny.technology URL; 'list' shows the user's existing links; 'revoke' kills one by id. Confirm before revoking.

action.description: What to do (default 'create' when messages given)

tiny.description: create: tiny name the conversation belongs to (default: tiny)

tools.name: tiny_events
tools.description: The user's activity feed — what happened while they were away: scheduled job results/errors, telegram messages, share views, tiny visits. Check after tiny_schedule creates jobs, or when the user asks 'what happened'. Pass since_id to poll incrementally.

since_id.description: Only events newer than this id (from a previous call)

tools.name: tiny_wallet
tools.description: The user's tiny.technology wallet. Actions: 'balance' (+ recent history), 'deposit_info' (how THIS deployment funds a wallet — read it before advising anything; the reply carries a `top_up` sentence naming the one valid route), 'faucet' (claim the free daily trial credit, where the deployment runs its own chain), 'pricing' (what a resource costs, e.g. a paid tiny), 'set_price' (price one of the user's own tinys, price_micro = USDC millionths, 0 = free), 'claim' (credit an on-chain deposit by tx hash). Balance is real USDC on Base on the public deployment and non-withdrawable trial credit on a testnet or self-hosted chain — never assume which; deposit_info says. NEVER tell a user to buy, bridge or exchange USDC before deposit_info confirms an external rail exists: on a self-hosted chain no exchange sells the token, so that advice costs them real money for credit this deployment cannot accept. Withdrawals and payout-address changes are deliberately NOT exposed here — use the web wallet.

price_micro.description: set_price: USDC millionths per message (1000000 = $1). 0 = free

network.description: claim: which network the deposit landed on (deposit_info.default_network; 'tiny' = this deployment's own chain)

tools.name: tiny_pay_quote
tools.description: Get a payment QUOTE for consulting a paid x402 service (e.g. a priced tiny) — probes the endpoint, and if it answers 402 returns a signed quote {quote, price_micro, network, payee, expires_at, summary}. NO money moves. Present the quote's summary to the user and STOP — only after they explicitly approve may tiny_pay_confirm be called with the same quote + message. Free endpoints answer immediately (response included, paid_micro: 0).

message.description: The message/task the payment buys — bound into the quote

max_spend_micro.description: Tighten the spend ceiling (USDC millionths); platform cap applies regardless

tools.name: tiny_pay_confirm
tools.description: EXECUTE a payment the user has EXPLICITLY approved — spends real USDC from their tiny wallet. Requires the exact quote from tiny_pay_quote and the same message it was quoted for (any mismatch is rejected). Quotes expire in ~5 minutes and are single-use. NEVER call this without the user's explicit, informed approval of the amount and payee in THIS conversation.

quote.description: The signed quote string from tiny_pay_quote

message.description: The identical message the quote was minted for

tools.name: tiny_send_message
tools.description: Send a direct message to another tiny.technology user — by @login or by one of their tiny's slugs. Delivery: their 💬 inbox on every tiny page, a push notification, and Telegram if they've paired a bot. Max 2000 chars.

to.description: Recipient: @login, login, or a tiny slug they own

tools.name: tiny_messages
tools.description: The user's DM inbox on tiny.technology. Without args: all threads (peer, last message, unread counts). With `with`: the full conversation with that user — opening it marks inbound messages read. Check when the user asks about messages or at session start if they expect DMs.

with.description: Peer @login to open that thread (marks read)

tools.name: tiny_follow
tools.description: Follow or unfollow a tiny.technology builder (by @login) — followers see the builder's PUBLIC memories in their feed (tiny_graph mode 'feed'). action 'check' reports current state without changing it. Unfollow closes the edge as history (bitemporal).

tools.name: tiny_delete_message
tools.description: Delete a DM the user sent, by message id (from tiny_messages thread view).

tools.name: tiny_devices
tools.description: The user's enrolled tiny devices (this CLI, phones, tiny-node daemons). 'list' shows id/name/kind/platform/online/last_seen. 'revoke' kills a device's token — its heartbeat/relay stops on the next 401. Enrollment isn't exposed here: devices enroll themselves on first run.

tools.name: tiny_model_config
tools.description: The user's cross-device BYO model config (which provider/model their tinys use everywhere they're signed in). 'get' is safe — the stored API key is never returned, only hasKey. 'set' updates provider/model fields; include apiKey ONLY to change it (omitted = stored key preserved, '' = cleared). The key is stored server-side by design — that's what syncs it across the user's devices.

action.description: get = read (key never returned) · set = update

baseUrl.description: set: OpenAI-compatible base URL (for custom hosts)

apiKey.description: set: ONLY to change the stored key ('' clears; omit to keep)

tools.name: tiny_model_providers
tools.description: The user's multi-provider BYO-model credential store ("pizza selection") — bedrock/anthropic/openai/… configured side by side and synced across every device they're signed into. 'list' is safe (keys never returned, only hasKey). 'set' upserts one provider (apiKey: omit=keep, ''=clear, value=replace; active:true makes it the live chat config). 'remove' deletes one. 'sync' pulls the cloud store into ~/.tiny/model-config.json and applies it to this process — how a CLI picks up config made on the web, and vice versa.

action.description: list = read (safe) · set = upsert one · remove = delete one · sync = pull cloud → local store

apiKey.description: set: ONLY to change the stored key ('' clears; omit to keep)

active.description: set: true → this provider becomes the active chat config

tools.name: tiny_archives
tools.description: Cloud archives of chat sessions (synced across the user's devices). 'list' → the user's archives; 'get' → one archive by id; 'save' → archive a conversation ({role, content} messages — the server redacts credentials); 'delete' → remove one by id.

tiny.description: save: tiny the conversation belongs to (default 'tiny')

tools.name: calendar_brief
tools.description: The user's calendar at a glance: zone + local clock, agenda for the next days (default 3) as compact lines, what is next up, pending booking requests, and whether public booking is on. Call this FIRST for any "what's on / am I busy / when is my next…" question and before creating an event so times land in the right zone. Read-only.

tools.name: calendar_events
tools.description: List or search the user's events. Give from+to (instants or YYYY-MM-DD) to list a window — recurring events are expanded into occurrences (same id, occurrence_start/occurrence_end) — or q to search titles/descriptions/locations. Returns event ids you need for calendar_update / calendar_delete / calendar_invite. Read-only.

from.description: Window start — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date

to.description: Window end — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date (max 62 days after from)

q.description: Free-text search instead of a window

tools.name: calendar_free
tools.description: Free windows in the user's calendar — "when am I free", "find 45 minutes with X this week". Defaults to their working hours (booking windows) between from and to (default today → +6 days); pass hours="09:00-18:00" and/or days="mon,tue" for an ad-hoc window ("any" = whole day). Adjacent free slots are merged into windows with local labels. All-day events do not block. Read-only.

to.description: Last local date YYYY-MM-DD inclusive (default from+6, max 62 days)

duration.description: Minimum minutes needed (default: booking slot length)

tools.name: calendar_create
tools.description: Create an event on the user's calendar. Required: title, start, end (ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date). Add attendees (emails) to make it an invite — then call calendar_invite to get the .ics / mailto / Google links to send; nothing is emailed automatically. Timed events that overlap an existing one are refused with reason "overlap" and the conflicts listed, unless force=true — tell the user what it collides with. Source is recorded as "agent". WRITES to the calendar.

start.description: Start — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date

end.description: End — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date

all_day.description: All-day event (implied when start is a bare date)

tz.description: IANA zone for this event when it differs from the calendar zone

rrule.description: Recurrence, RFC 5545 without the RRULE: prefix — FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY|YEARLY[;INTERVAL=n][;COUNT=n][;UNTIL=YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ][;BYDAY=MO,TU]. Empty string clears it.

attendees.description: Full attendee list (replaces the existing list on update)

email.description: Attendee email — this is where the .ics invite goes

force.description: Create even when it overlaps an existing event

tools.name: calendar_update
tools.description: Change an existing event (id from calendar_events/calendar_brief): move it, rename it, set location/notes, change attendees or status. Only the fields you pass change. Bumps the iCalendar SEQUENCE so re-sent invites update in guests' calendars. status="cancelled" keeps the event visible as cancelled; use calendar_delete to remove it. WRITES to the calendar.

start.description: Start — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date

end.description: End — ISO-8601 instant with offset/Z (e.g. 2026-10-05T14:00:00-04:00) OR a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day LOCAL date; for all-day the LAST day (inclusive)

all_day.description: All-day event (implied when start is a bare date)

tz.description: IANA zone for this event when it differs from the calendar zone

rrule.description: Recurrence, RFC 5545 without the RRULE: prefix — FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY|YEARLY[;INTERVAL=n][;COUNT=n][;UNTIL=YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ][;BYDAY=MO,TU]. Empty string clears it.

attendees.description: Full attendee list (replaces the existing list on update)

email.description: Attendee email — this is where the .ics invite goes

force.description: Allow the new time to overlap other events (pass both start and end to move)

tools.name: calendar_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: delete an event by id. Soft-delete: the iOS/web sync sees a tombstone and removes it everywhere. Confirm with the user first when the event has attendees or came from a booking (their guest will not be told automatically — offer to send the cancellation via calendar_invite BEFORE deleting, it emits METHOD:CANCEL once status is cancelled).

tools.name: calendar_invite
tools.description: Everything needed to send an invitation for an event: the public .ics link (anyone can add it to their calendar), a prefilled mailto: to all attendees carrying that link (open it and the user's mail app sends the invite — tiny sends no email itself), a Google Calendar link, and the raw ics text. ORGANIZER is <login>@tiny.technology so guests' Accept/Decline replies flow back into the attendee statuses. For a cancelled event the ics is METHOD:CANCEL.

tools.name: calendar_bookings
tools.description: People booking the user's time from their tiny profile (https://tiny.technology/@login). action=list shows bookings (status filter pending|upcoming|all); accept/decline decide a pending request (id from the list) — decline cancels the underlying event. Booking requests also arrive as events with source "booking".

tools.name: calendar_settings
tools.description: Read or change the calendar itself: name, zone (tz), colour, and the public booking page — booking_settings { booking_enabled, windows {mon..sun: [["09:00","17:00"]]}, slot_minutes, buffer_minutes, min_notice_hours, max_per_day, horizon_days, booking_questions[], auto_confirm }. Pass only what changes (booking_settings merges). action=feed returns the private webcal:// subscription URL (Apple/Google Calendar can subscribe); action=rotate_feed invalidates it. Turning booking on makes the user bookable by ANYONE at their profile URL — confirm first.

tools.name: calendar_view
tools.description: SHOW the user's calendar as an interactive card (day / week / month / agenda) — the typed kind:"calendar" payload the tiny web/iOS chat renders inline; over MCP you get the same JSON (events + range + filters + a "note" summary). Call this whenever the user wants to SEE their calendar, invites, a day, a week or a month — "show my week", "what's on today" (view=day), "this month", "show my invites" (kinds=["invites"]), "what needs my reply" (kinds=["needs_reply"]), "find the dentist appointment" (q). Use calendar_brief instead for a purely spoken one-sentence answer. Read-only.

view.description: default week; day for "today", agenda for "what is coming up" and invite lists

date.description: Anchor: YYYY-MM-DD local date or an instant; default today. "next week" = today+7 in the calendar zone

from.description: Explicit window start (instant or YYYY-MM-DD) — overrides the view range (implies agenda unless view given)

to.description: Explicit window end (exclusive instant, or an inclusive YYYY-MM-DD)

q.description: Search titles/descriptions/locations instead of a date window

attendee.description: Only events with this guest (email or name fragment)

kinds.description: invites = has guests · needs_reply = invites the user has not answered · bookings = booked via their profile · all_day · timed

tools.name: site_create
tools.description:
Create a new website (versioned static site + optional tiny.js app) and get its URL. Give it index.html plus separate css/js files and assets/ for images (svg inline is fine); the site is live immediately at the returned url — answer the user with the URL, never paste whole HTML into chat. Version 1 is the files you pass (template:'page' scaffolds index.html/css/js when files is empty). Result is a site card {kind:'site', url, viewer_url, version, warnings[]}. Later edits: site_write (partial — only changed files). Visibility: public (listed on the profile) | unlisted | private (viewer only through tiny). WRITES (creates a site).
tiny.js — the page talks to this site's tiny (add ONE tag, everything below is available as window.tiny):
  <script src="/_tiny/tiny.js"></script>
  await tiny.ready                           // {site, visitor, permissions}; rejects {code:'isolation_required'} on a shared origin
  tiny.visitor                               // {id, anonymous, login?, name?}   tiny.signIn() / tiny.signOut()   (popup, "Sign in with tiny")
  tiny.state.get(k) / set(k,v) / delete(k) / list(prefix) / push(k,item) / subscribe(k|prefix, cb)
      keys:  top-level = owner/agent write, everyone reads ·  v/<visitorId>/… = private to that visitor (use tiny.visitor.id)
             shared/… = visitors may write when permissions.state_shared (guestbook/votes → use push(), FIFO 1000)
  tiny.submit(dataOrForm, {form:'contact'})  // → owner's inbox as kind site_submit (+ automation if enabled); or <form data-tiny-submit="contact">
  tiny.ask(text, {onToken})                  // streamed answer from the site's tiny — needs permissions.ask (spends the owner's budget)
  tiny.on('state'|'version'|'message', cb)   // live via SSE; a new version auto-reloads the page (toast) unless tiny.config.autoReload=false
  tiny.book()                                // owner's booking page (permissions.book)
  tiny.ui.chat({mount:'#chat'})              // drop-in streaming chat widget      tiny.ui.signInButton({mount:'#login'})
  declarative: <div data-tiny-chat> <form data-tiny-submit="name"> <span data-tiny-state="key"> <button data-tiny-signin>
RULES: for anything interactive (forms, chat, counters, guestbook, per-visitor progress, live data) use tiny.js — never invent a
backend, never call third-party form/analytics/chat services. Values are JSON ≤ 64 KB, 2k keys/site. Paths under _tiny/ are
reserved (400). template:'app'|'chat'|'form' ships working tiny.js pages to EDIT rather than write from scratch. When you enable
a permission (ask, state_shared, book) via site_update, TELL the user what it allows and what it costs.

name.description: Human name, e.g. "Portfolio" — the slug is derived unless given

template.description: When files is empty: blank = no files · page = static page (hero + sections, tiny footer) · app = index+app.js+style.css wired to tiny.js (shared guestbook, ask widget, contact form, sign-in; enables ask + state_shared) · chat = full-page chat with your tiny (enables ask) · form = contact/registration form → owner inbox via tiny.submit. Default page.

path.description: Relative path, e.g. index.html, css/site.css, js/app.js, assets/logo.svg (no .., no leading /, _tiny/ reserved)

content_base64.description: Binary content as base64 (png/jpg/mp4/woff2…), ≤2 MB — bigger files: tell the user to upload in the site UI

delete.description: true removes the file in this version

permissions.description: tiny.js permissions to enable (ask, state_shared, book…) — TELL the user what each allows

tools.name: site_write
tools.description: Edit an existing site: PARTIAL update — pass only the files that change (new content, or delete:true); untouched files stay. Creates a new version and returns the site card with added/changed/removed + warnings. Pass base=<version you read> to be safe: a 409 means someone wrote in between → site_read the manifest and retry with the new base. Read a file with site_read before rewriting one you did not just write. WRITES a new version. (tiny.js rules: see site_create.)

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

message.description: What changed, like a commit message

path.description: Relative path, e.g. index.html, css/site.css, js/app.js, assets/logo.svg (no .., no leading /, _tiny/ reserved)

content_base64.description: Binary content as base64 (png/jpg/mp4/woff2…), ≤2 MB — bigger files: tell the user to upload in the site UI

delete.description: true removes the file in this version

base.description: The version you are editing on top of (default: current)

tools.name: site_read
tools.description: Read a site: without path → meta + manifest (every file with size/mime) + current version; with path → that file's text (≤64 KB, else truncated) — binaries return size/mime only. version= reads an older version. Always read before editing a file you did not just write. Read-only.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_list
tools.description: The user's sites (name, public_id, visibility, version, url, updated) — their own AND sites shared with them (role: primary | owner = co-owner | editor; owner.login says whose). Use it to resolve 'my portfolio site' before site_write/site_read. Read-only.

tools.name: site_versions
tools.description: Version history of a site, newest first (version, message, author, +added/~changed/−removed). Pick one for site_rollback. Read-only.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_rollback
tools.description: MUTATIVE: restore a site to an earlier version. Non-destructive in effect: creates a NEW version whose files equal v<version> (message "rollback to vN"), so it can itself be undone — but the live site changes immediately; confirm with the user.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_update
tools.description: Change site settings (not files): name, description, visibility, slug (→ new public id + URL), entry file, and tiny.js knobs — permissions (partial merge: ask, identity, state_public_read, state_shared, agent_state_write, submit, events, book, pay, realtime), agent_slug (which tiny answers /_tiny/ask; null = yours), automation (off | notify | agent — agent runs a one-shot job on YOUR rail per submit/event, 50/site/day), automation_note (standing instruction), ask_daily_limit. When you enable a permission, TELL the user what it allows and what it costs (ask spends their budget). WRITES settings.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: delete a site (soft: hidden immediately, purged after 7 days). confirm must equal the site's public_id — ask the user first.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_state_get
tools.description: Read a site's tiny.js state: one key, or list keys by prefix/scope (all | owner | shared | visitors). Keys: top-level = owner/agent write, everyone reads · v/<visitorId>/… = one visitor's private data · shared/… = visitor-writable when permissions.state_shared. Values are JSON ≤64 KB. This is how you see what visitors submitted/pushed (guestbook, votes, progress). Read-only.

site.description: Which site: id, public_id (slug-8hex), your slug, or its URL. Sites shared with you (you are co-owner or editor) work the same way.

tools.name: site_state_set
tools.description: WRITES a site's tiny.js state key (any namespace, as the owner): the page sees it live via tiny.state.subscribe / tiny.on('state'). Use it to publish data to a page (menu, scores, announcements) without a new version. push=true appends to a list key (FIFO 1000). Keys: top-level = owner/agent write, everyone reads · v/<visitorId>/… = one visitor's private data · shared/… = visitor-writable when permissions.state_shared. Values are JSON ≤64 KB.

tools.name: use_npm
tools.description:
Use ANY npm package as a native tool — install on demand, reflect its surface, call it. Sandbox: ~/.tiny/npm (survives upgrades). Actions:
- search (query) — find packages on registry.npmjs.org
- info (package) — registry metadata: latest version, description, deps
- install (package) — npm install into the sandbox (spec ok: pkg@1.2.3)
- inspect (package) — import it, list real exports with signatures (do this BEFORE call)
- call (package, export='path.to.fn', args=[...], construct=false) — invoke one export, JSON in/out
- run (code) — arbitrary ESM code, sandbox packages importable: await import('pkg')
- installed — what's in the sandbox
- remove (package)
Workflow: search → install → inspect → call. Prefer call; use run when glue is needed (streams, callbacks, chained APIs).

export.description: dotted export path, e.g. 'default' or 'promises.readFile'; empty = module default

tools.name: use_openapi
tools.description:
Any HTTP API described by an OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.0 spec (JSON or YAML) — Stripe, GitHub, Twilio, OpenAI, Kubernetes, your own service. Load the spec once, then call operations by name with real parameter validation and stored auth.

Actions:
- load (spec_url, alias?) — read a spec from a URL, local path, or GitHub blob URL. Returns the API's shape (base URL, operation count, auth schemes, tag groups) — NOT every operation, because big specs have hundreds.
- search (query, alias?, limit?) — find operations by intent: 'create charge', 'list issues', 'GET /pets'. Start here.
- describe (operation, alias?) — one operation in full: every parameter with location/required/type/enum, the request body's actual fields (with $refs resolved), response shape. Read this before calling something new.
- call (operation, alias?, params?, body?) — make the call. params is a JSON object of parameter names; path/query/header/cookie placement comes from the spec. Missing required parameters or unknown names are refused BEFORE the request, with the closest real name.
- raw (method, path, alias?, params?, body?) — an endpoint the spec doesn't describe (or no spec at all: pass a full URL as path).
- auth (alias, …) — store credentials: api_key='…' | token='…' | username+password | auth_flow='authorization_code'|'client_credentials' with client_id/client_secret (opens a browser for the first). Credentials are bound to the API's host and refused elsewhere.
- tokens / forget (alias) — what's stored (redacted) / delete it.
- schemas (alias, name?) — the spec's models.
- list — which specs this machine has loaded.

spec_url.description: URL, local path, or GitHub blob URL of the spec (load)

alias.description: which loaded API — defaults to the only one, or searches all

allow_host.description: additionally authorise this host for the credential

tools.name: use_memory
tools.description:
🧠 use_memory — durable memory on THIS machine, no account needed.

  save    text='…' [title=] [tags=] [meta=] [supersedes=]  write a fact down
  recall  query='…' [tags=] [since=] [limit=]              find it by intent
  list    [tags=] [limit=]                                 newest first
  get     id=mem_…                                         one memory in full
  forget  id=mem_…                                         delete one
  tags | stats | help

Save what stays true: preferences, decisions, names, how this machine is set
up, what went wrong last time. Recall BEFORE assuming you don't know something
about the user — the query is plain words, never a query language, so no
phrasing can fail. The store is a file the user can read: ~/.tiny/memory.

tiny_recall searches your tiny account's memory graph across devices and is the
better place for facts that should follow the user. This one always works.

title.description: short label — derived from the text if omitted

tags.description: comma-separated tags (save, or a filter for recall/list)

supersedes.description: id of the memory this replaces (save)

since.description: only memories updated after this date, e.g. 2026-08-01

tools.name: use_image
tools.description:
👀 SEE an image file — the picture itself lands in your context, not a description of it.
- view (path | paths[] | url) — attach up to 6 images. A directory path attaches its first 6 images (use offset to page). max_edge (default 1568) shrinks big photos; nothing is ever upscaled. HEIC/TIFF/BMP are converted on the fly (macOS sips or ImageMagick). Files on disk are never modified.
- info (path) — format (from bytes), dimensions, size; for a directory: every image with its dimensions, no pixels attached (free).
Phone photos are 4000px+ and get resampled to max_edge; pass max_edge=600 to skim many cheaply, or view one at a time at the default for detail.

max_edge.description: longest edge in px after resampling (default 1568)

offset.description: directory paging: skip this many images

tools.name: use_integrations
tools.description:
Connect this device to Google, Spotify, Telegram, WhatsApp — the agent-side of `tiny-tech connect`. Walk the user through onboarding conversationally. Actions:
- status — every service: ready / partial / missing, with what connecting unlocks
- guide (service) — exact setup steps to read back to the user (where to click, what to paste)
- save (service + credentials) — store what the user pasted (~/.tiny/integrations.json, 0600). google: client_json_path OR client_id+client_secret · spotify: client_id+client_secret [+redirect_uri] · telegram: token (verified before storing)
- login (service) — start browser OAuth for google/spotify (needs prior save). The user finishes in the browser.
- forget (service) — remove a stored connection
Secrets are never echoed back. WhatsApp linking is guide-only (QR needs a terminal).

tools.name: use_device
tools.description: Reach the user's OTHER enrolled devices — laptops/daemons from `npx tiny-tech`, phones, and `endpoint` devices (a 3D printer, a robot at its own API). action:'list' shows each device with online presence AND the `capabilities` it declares — match the task to a device that declares the power it needs, and never tell the user a device lacks something without checking that list first. Endpoint devices show online:null (reachability unknown until invoked), not offline. action:'invoke' sends a prompt to a device — its LOCAL agent executes (real shell, real files, its own tools) and the answer comes back here; it waits up to ~45s, and a slower task returns pending:true with an envelope_id instead of failing (the device keeps working and the user gets a push when it finishes). For a clearly long task or an explicit 'in the background', pass wait:false — the envelope_id comes back immediately. action:'result' with that envelope_id fetches the finished result — kept ~24 hours and re-readable. If the device made images during the turn (e.g. a Mac screenshotting its own screen), they come back as images you can SEE plus hosted URLs. Only the owner's devices are reachable; prefer online devices. This machine is itself enrolled — asking it to invoke itself is refused (just do the task locally).

device_id.description: Target device id (from list). Required for invoke.

prompt.description: What the device agent should do. Required for invoke.

envelope_id.description: Envelope id from a pending invoke (or a batch_*/task_* ticket — every kind redeems identically). Required for action:'result'.

wait.description: invoke only (default true): wait up to ~45s for the answer. false = fire-and-forget — return the pending ticket immediately.
